sources.entry: Java: _Building Your Own Kafka-like System From Scratch: A Step-by-Step Guide_

summary.one_liner: A tutorial-style Java project for building a simplified Kafka-like distributed messaging system (SimpleKafka) step by step, with ZooKeeper-based coordination, brokers, and clients.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a guide for building SimpleKafka incrementally over seven stages: project setup, a core protocol layer, ZooKeeper integration, a storage layer, a broker, a client library, and higher-level producer and consumer APIs, followed by a testing stage. It says the stages are meant to be followed alongside a separate step-by-step Medium article, so much of the detail lives outside this README. The testing section shows how to compile with Maven, start ZooKeeper, launch three broker instances on different ports, and run a producer and a consumer against a test topic. It also lists concepts to observe while testing: partition distribution, leader and follower replication, controller election through ZooKeeper, log segments and offset indices, and the binary client-broker protocol.
use_cases: build a toy message broker for study
understand partition leader and follower replication
practice distributed systems design in Java
run a local multi-broker messaging demo with ZooKeeper
how_to_run: zkServer start (or zookeeper-server-start with a zk.cfg file on port 2181)
java -cp target/simple-kafka-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar com.simplekafka.broker.SimpleKafkaBroker 1 localhost 9091 2181 (repeat for brokers 2 and 3 on ports 9092 and 9093)
notable: Staged build-it-yourself curriculum, from project setup through producer and consumer APIs
Brokers coordinate through ZooKeeper, with controller election and leader failover
Includes a custom binary client-broker protocol
Companion Medium article is referenced for the detailed walkthrough
caveats: Stage-by-stage instructions are not in the README; it points to an external Medium article for them
Requires a running ZooKeeper instance, and the README gives several alternative startup commands that depend on local installation
No license is stated in the README
